_meta.purpose: Seed constructions for per-level metric validation. Each family fixes some linguistic levels and varies exactly one, so ground truth is known at every level rather than only at the level under test.
_meta.caveat: Hand-authored for this repository. Ground truth is an authored construct and has not been validated by external annotators; see README.

syntactic_alternations._doc: One proposition realised through n syntactic structures. Semantics is held constant, syntax varies. A syntactic metric must report ~n; a semantic metric must report ~1.

realisations: The meal was prepared by the chef.
It was the chef who prepared the meal.
What the chef prepared was the meal.
The roof was damaged by the storm.
It was the storm that damaged the roof.
What damaged the roof was the storm.

sets.proposition: I sent the letter to my brother
realisations: I sent the letter to my brother.
I sent my brother the letter.
The letter was sent to my brother by me.
My brother was sent the letter by me.
It was my brother that I sent the letter to.
New engineers were hired by the company.
It was new engineers that the company hired.
What the company hired was new engineers.

sets.proposition: the team built the bridge quickly
realisations: The team built the bridge quickly.
The bridge was built quickly by the team.
Quickly, the team built the bridge.
It was quickly that the team built the bridge.
What the team did was build the bridge quickly.
The answer was known to the student.
It was the student who knew the answer.
What the student knew was the answer.

syntactic_frames._doc: k syntactic frames x m lexicalisations. Within a frame the structure and the POS sequence are identical while the content differs. A syntactic metric must report ~k; a semantic metric must report ~k*m.

frames.pattern: DET ADJ NOUN VERB DET NOUN
lexicalisations: The tall boy kicked the ball.
A red car struck the fence.
The old woman watered the garden.
That young girl painted the wall.

frames.pattern: SCONJ DET NOUN VERB PUNCT DET NOUN VERB
lexicalisations: When the rain stopped, the children played.
After the meeting ended, the manager left.
Because the road flooded, the bus stopped.
Before the show started, the crowd cheered.

frames.pattern: PRON VERB SCONJ DET NOUN AUX ADJ
lexicalisations: She believes that the plan is sound.
He knows that the answer is wrong.
They think that the price is high.
I doubt that the story is true.

frames.pattern: DET NOUN ADP DET NOUN AUX VERB
lexicalisations: The book on the table was missing.
The keys in the drawer were stolen.
The painting in the hall was damaged.
The letter on the desk was opened.

frames.pattern: VERB DET NOUN CCONJ VERB DET NOUN
lexicalisations: Open the door and close the window.
Take the money and leave the room.
Read the book and write the essay.
Boil the water and add the salt.

frames.pattern: PRON VERB DET NOUN ADP DET NOUN
lexicalisations: There was a crack in the ceiling.
There is a stain on the carpet.
There was a gap in the fence.
There is a knot in the rope.

morphological_templates._doc: Same content realised with different part-of-speech sequences (nominalisation, adjectival, verbal). Content is held roughly constant while the POS sequence varies. A morphological metric must report ~n; a semantic metric must report ~1.

realisations: His refusal of the offer was final.
The offer was refused by him.
The army's destruction of the city was total.
The city was destroyed by the army.
The city lay destroyed by the army.
The arrival of the train was late.
A decision was reached by the committee.

pos_identical_structure_different._doc: Pairs with the same part-of-speech sequence but different grammatical relations (object complement vs ditransitive). A morphological metric should collapse these toward 1; a syntactic metric should separate them. This is the sharpest available test that the two levels are not measuring the same thing. Every pair here was checked to produce genuinely different spaCy dependency parses -- see surface_parse_blind for the ones that do not.

sets.pattern: PRON VERB DET NOUN DET NOUN
realisations: He gave the boy the book.
He called the boy a liar.

sets.pattern: DET NOUN VERB DET NOUN ADJ
realisations: The men painted the house red.
The men left the house today.

surface_parse_blind._doc: Distinctions a surface dependency parse cannot represent. spaCy assigns these pairs byte-identical dependency labels and heads, so control/raising and PP-attachment differences are invisible to any metric built on such a parse. Retained as a recorded limitation rather than a failing test: the expectation is that both syntactic and morphological metrics collapse them to 1.0. Separating them would require semantic role labelling, not a better tree distance.

realisations: The chicken is ready to eat.
The chicken is likely to eat.
She watched the man with the telescope.
She watched the man with the beard.
sets.note: instrument vs modifier PP; spaCy attaches both to the verb

rhythmic_meters._doc: k metrical patterns x m lines. Within a meter the stress contour is fixed while words and content differ. A rhythmic metric must report ~k; a semantic metric must report ~k*m.

lines: The clock upon the wall was slow.
A bird beneath the bridge has flown.
The road beyond the hill was long.
A light within the room was dim.
Cannon to right of them thundered.
Half of the company faltered and scattered.
And the sheen of their spears was like stars.
It was late in the night when he came.
In the blink of an eye it was gone.
On the edge of the world there is light.

phonemic_oronyms._doc: Sentence pairs that are near-homophonic but orthographically and semantically distinct. A phonemic metric must collapse these toward 1; a semantic metric must report ~n. Supply is inherently limited: full-sentence homophony is rare in English.

realisations: That was a grade A result.
That was a grey day result.
The debate concerned youth in Asia.
She had an aim in mind.
She had a name in mind.
That is the stuff he needs.
That is the stuff he kneads.

phonemic_minimal_pairs._doc: Sets differing in a single phoneme in the head word, holding syntax and POS sequence fixed. A phonemic metric must separate these; the separation should be small relative to phonemically distant sets, giving a graded rather than binary test.

sets.note: control set: same frame, phonemically distant heads

morphological_inflection._doc: k inflectional patterns x m lexicalisations, one syntactic frame throughout. Only the verb's inflection varies within a pattern, so a morphological metric must report ~k. Invisible to UPOS, where every form is VERB -- this family exists to test the fine-grained tagset.

lexicalisations: The worker walks to the site.
The teacher speaks to the class.
The engineer drives to the plant.
The farmer rides to the market.
The worker walked to the site.
The teacher spoke to the class.
The engineer drove to the plant.
The farmer rode to the market.
The worker is walking to the site.
The teacher is speaking to the class.
The engineer is driving to the plant.
The farmer is riding to the market.
The worker has walked to the site.
The teacher has spoken to the class.
The engineer has driven to the plant.
The farmer has ridden to the market.

constituency_contrasts._doc: Phrase-structure contrasts, each verified against spaCy+benepar before inclusion. Note the measured result: dependency parsing separates most of these *better* than constituency does. Only coordination scope favours the constituency metric, and NP-internal bracketing is invisible to both parsers. Retained so that claim rests on data.

realisations: They hired old men and women.
They hired old men and old women.
sets.note: shared vs distributed adjective scope; con 0.769, dep 0.875

realisations: The rat the cat chased died.
The cat chased the rat that died.
He knows that the answer is wrong.
He knows the answer that is wrong.
The book on the table in the room vanished.
The book vanished on the table today.
She met the French history teacher.
She met the tall history teacher.
sets.note: both report 1.000: neither parser resolves the bracketing

rhythmic_stress_pairs._doc: English noun/verb stress alternations: the same orthographic word carries different stress depending on category (a REcord / to reCORD). Lexically near-identical, so a rhythmic metric should separate what a lexical one cannot.

realisations: She kept a record of the meeting.
She had to record the meeting.
They opened the present at noon.
They will present the report at noon.

phonemic_graded._doc: Three tiers of phonological distance at a fixed syntactic frame, so the phonemic metric can be scored on an ordering rather than a binary. tier1 < tier2 < tier3 is the claim; absolute values are not the point.
